correctness.rationale: Every square-zero equation is derived from path multiplication, the four closed component candidates are exhaustive, the first two have irreducible dense 7-dimensional opens with boundary dimension at most six, and the other two are affine seven-spaces. The three disjoint strata calculate [X]=L^6(4L-3). The characteristic-seven dihedral isomorphism is constructive via a sign-anti-invariant generator. The packaged verifier separately computes 6561 F3 points after two free variables and the F7 generator change; finite testing is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The entire reduced square-zero geometry of the natural smallest cyclic Nakayama algebra at Loewy seven is determined: four equidimensional geometric components, exact motivic class over all fields of characteristic not two, and uniform finite-field counts. The characteristic-seven modular dihedral group algebra gives a classical group-ring realization of the same invariant. This is not merely finite enumeration: the explicit component decomposition explains the point-count polynomial and distinguishes this Loewy-seven two-cycle regime from previously studied fourth truncations.
